topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors as Spatial Guides
target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors as Spatial Guides
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

sections.title: Defining the Vector: Movement in Space
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a vector as an ordered pair representing magnitude and direction, distinct from a single point. Visualize this as an arrow starting at the origin (0,0) and ending at a specific coordinate.
sections.example: A 'Robot Dog' starting at the charging station (0,0) moves to position (3, 2). The vector v = [3, 2] describes this displacement.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Path
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar (a real number) changes its length but keeps its direction (or reverses it). Use a scaling animation to show the vector growing or shrinking along the same line.
sections.example: The 'Robot Dog' runs twice as fast, effectively doubling its displacement vector: 2 * [3, 2] = [6, 4].

sections.title: Vector Addition: Combining Forces
sections.content: Introduce vector addition using the 'Tip-to-Tail' method. Visually demonstrate placing the start of the second vector at the tip of the first to find the final resultant position.
sections.example: The 'Robot Dog' first moves [3, 2] to find a ball, then moves [1, -3] to find a bone. The total displacement is [3+1, 2-3] = [4, -1].

sections.title: Linear Combinations: The Basis of Space
sections.content: Explain how any point in a 2D plane can be reached by combining the basis vectors (i = [1,0] and j = [0,1]). This serves as the foundation for defining span and coordinate systems.
sections.example: Think of the 'Robot Dog' moving on a grid. To reach any point (x, y), it simply moves 'x' units along the x-axis and 'y' units along the y-axis, representing the combination: x[1,0] + y[0,1].

storyboard.title: Defining the Vector: Movement in Space
lecture_lines: Vectors are arrows, not just single points.
They represent both magnitude and direction.
Picture a robot starting at origin (0,0).

storyboard.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Path
lecture_lines: Scalar multiplication changes a vector's length.
It stretches or shrinks along the line.
The direction remains the same or reverses.

storyboard.title: Vector Addition: Combining Forces
lecture_lines: Vector addition combines two distinct movements.
Use the tip-to-tail method for vectors.
Place the start at the previous tip.
animations: Show two vectors v1 and v2 on screen. (#FFFFFF)
Slide v2 tip to meet v1 tail. (#00FF00)
Draw result vector from v1 tail to v2 tip. (#0000FF)

storyboard.title: Linear Combinations: The Basis of Space
lecture_lines: Basis vectors i and j span space.
Combine them to reach any point.
Every location is a linear combination.
animations: Display unit vectors i and j at origin. (#FFFFFF)
Scale i and j by scalars to form grid. (#FFFF00)
Highlight a point reached by linear combination. (#FF00FF)
